tasks.short: Examine the travel document, capture data and biometrics, read database hits, interview the traveller, decide on admission and record the entry.

steps.what: Officer examines passports and visas for signs of forgery
Officer captures passport data, fingerprints and face image at the booth
Officer reads database hits on the traveller and the document
Officer interviews persons about the purpose of travel, length of stay and means
Officer decides on eligibility for admission
Officer stamps the passport with entry date and place

tasks.design: Non-EU travellers capture their passport data, fingerprints and face image at self-service kiosks before the booth, and the border system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the officer the capture and any database hits; the officer checks the capture instead of taking it. When the officer admits a traveller, the system writes the entry to the EU's electronic entry and exit register instead of a stamp. Examining documents, the interview and the decision stay with the officer; no AI scores travellers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data and biometrics were captured at the booth and entries were stamped by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: The EU's electronic entry and exit register and self-service kiosks at border crossings.
tasks.still_hard: Kiosks fail on worn passports and some travellers; forged documents need a trained eye.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a traveller's story does not fit the ticket in their hand.

reach.learn: Whether kiosks shorten time per traveller at the booth.

evidence.claim: The EU Entry/Exit System records non-EU travellers' entries and exits electronically with biometrics, replacing passport stamps.
AI used at borders, such as for examining visa and residence applications, is high-risk under the AI Act.
Fingerprints and face images are biometric special-category data.

assumptions: Boundary: from the traveller at the booth to the recorded entry; asylum requests are outside.
Input contract: watch lists and visa data from EU and national border systems; kiosks run by the border agency; fallback is capture at the booth.
Examining, the interview and the decision do not change.
EU citizens get a document check only and gain less.
unknowns: Share of non-EU travellers at this crossing.
research_questions: Does time per traveller at the booth fall?

already_counted.description: Officer checks kiosk captures and resolves mismatches.

incremental.description: Officer helps travellers when a kiosk fails.

approvals.approved_version: The admission decision taken by the officer in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Crossings with mostly EU travellers gain little.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select what to inspect, read scanner images, search to locate contraband, seize and seal it, record the seizure, give the owner a receipt and file the case.

steps.what: Officer selects vehicles, containers and travellers for inspection from risk flags and own observation
Officer examines scanner images of vehicles and containers
Officer searches vehicles, aircraft, boats and luggage to locate contraband
Officer seizes the undeclared merchandise and seals it in evidence bags
Officer writes the seizure report on a paper form
Officer writes a seizure receipt for the owner by hand
Officer copies the seizure into the customs case system

tasks.design: The officer records the seizure on a tablet in the customs case system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with photos, seal numbers and fixed fields for goods and quantities. Once the officer confirms the record, the system prints the receipt for the owner and opens the case without retyping. Selecting, reading images, searching and seizing stay with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Seizures were written on paper forms, receipts by hand and both retyped later.
tasks.enabler_now: Tablet forms with photos and printers in the inspection area are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Finding contraband is skill; the record must keep the chain of custody intact.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing the panel that sits a centimetre too far from the frame.

reach.learn: Whether seal numbers in the record cut errors at intake.

evidence.claim: Tablet forms with photos and fixed fields can record seizures and print receipts.
Seizure records can be evidence in court and must show the chain of custody.

assumptions: Boundary: from selection to the opened case; storage and destruction of goods are outside.
Input contract: risk flags from the customs risk system; goods lists set by the customs administration; fallback is paper forms.
Selecting, searching and seizing do not change.
No AI reads scanner images in this design.
research_questions: Do seizure records reach the case team complete?

incremental.description: Officer learns the tablet seizure form.

approvals.approved_version: The seizure record as completed by the officer in s5; corrections need a new confirmation before a receipt is printed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is searching in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain rules to travellers, classify goods for shippers, look up duty measures, answer e-mailed questions with quoted guidance and answer calls.

steps.what: Officer explains laws and regulations to travelers at the border
Officer classifies the shipper's goods under a commodity code
Officer looks up duty measures and national rates for the code
Officer writes replies to shippers' and manufacturers' e-mailed questions

loop.input: The shipper's e-mailed question, the duty measures from s3 and the official customs guidance pages.
loop.output: A draft reply that quotes the matching guidance passage and the duty measure, each with its link.
loop.check: Code checks that every quoted passage matches the guidance page word for word and every rate matches the looked-up measure; the officer reads, edits and sends every reply.
loop.stop: One draft per question; no matching guidance means the officer writes the reply.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions come in free text about many goods and procedures; a fixed FAQ does not match them.

steps.what: Officer answers phone questions from shippers about procedures

tasks.design: Once the officer picks a commodity code, the customs desk tool shows the EU duty measures and national rates for it from the EU tariff database ({GOV_PORTAL}). For e-mailed questions, a bounded step drafts a reply that quotes the official guidance and the measure, checked word for word by code, and the officer edits and sends it. Explaining rules at the border, classifying goods and phone calls stay with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measures were looked up by hand and every e-mail was written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: EU duty measures are published daily in a database, and language models can match free text to guidance.
tasks.still_hard: Classifying goods is judgement; a wrong answer can cost a shipper money.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining calmly to a traveller why their goods are held.
tasks.altitude: The officer checks quoted replies instead of writing every one.

reach.learn: Whether quoted replies cut follow-up questions.

evidence.claim: TARIC holds EU duty measures and is sent daily to national customs.
Only a binding tariff information decision binds customs on classification; e-mailed answers do not.

assumptions: Boundary: from questions to answers given; formal rulings are outside.
Input contract: guidance pages kept by the national customs administration; duty measures from the EU tariff database plus national rates; fallback is manual lookup and writing.
Explaining in person, classifying and calls do not change.
Shippers' time is outside the officer's savings.
research_questions: How many e-mailed questions match a guidance passage?

already_counted.description: Officer reads and edits each drafted reply.

incremental.description: Customs administration keeps guidance pages current for quoting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Posts where most questions come in person save less.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide to prosecute, gather the case file, fill in details, write and sign the report, send it to the prosecutor and partners, and cooperate on investigations.

steps.what: Officer weighs the evidence to institute a civil or criminal prosecution
Officer collects seizure records, photos and documents into the case file
Officer types suspect and goods details into the official report
Officer writes the narrative of the official report
Officer checks the case file and signs the official report
Officer e-mails the case file to the prosecutor and partner agencies
Officer cooperates with police and other law enforcement agencies in joint investigations

tasks.design: When the officer opens a case, the customs case system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) links the seizure records, photos and documents already held and fills suspect and goods details into the official report. The narrative stays the officer's own writing: a randomised trial found AI-drafted police reports were not written faster. After the officer signs, the system sends the file through a secure, logged channel to the prosecutor and named partner agencies. Deciding to prosecute and joint investigations stay with people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case files were gathered by hand from several places and e-mailed.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems link records per case and share files through logged channels.
tasks.still_hard: Sharing with partners needs a legal basis per agency; the narrative must be the officer's own.
tasks.human_edge: Building trust with police partners so a case moves.

evidence.claim: A randomised trial found AI-drafted police reports were not written faster.
Case systems can link records per case and share files through logged channels.
Predicting offences solely from profiling is banned under the AI Act; this design adds no scoring.

assumptions: Boundary: from the seizure case to joint investigation; the prosecutor's decision is outside.
Input contract: seizure case entries made by officers at the border; partner list and sharing rules set by the customs administration's legal team; fallback is e-mail.
Prosecutor and partner time is outside the officer's savings.
Deciding, writing the narrative and cooperation do not change.
unknowns: Cases sent to the prosecutor per month.
research_questions: Do prosecutors ask for missing documents less often?

already_counted.description: Officer checks the linked case file is complete.

incremental.description: Legal team keeps the partner sharing list current.

approvals.approved_version: The case file as signed by the officer in s5; any change needs a new signature before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Complex cases need long narratives and much joint work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The customs officer keeps examining, searching, interviewing and deciding; capture, stamps, retyping and file gathering shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An officer who spends more of the shift on inspection and less on forms.
